title: Negotiating with Joe Glaser and the Bermuda debut
summary: Glaser haggled over prices, and Moore's plunger solo on 'Wabash Blues' in Bermuda impressed Lucille Armstrong.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: So I want to see Glaser and I'm in the office with Joe Glaser and Joe Glaser says to me, " I don't know, Chief, you play with the big society orchestras, I don't know if I can afford you. Do you want to play with Louie?" I says, " I always want to play with

Louie. Who don't? A great opportunity. He said, "Well, what would you want for one-nighters?" I told him the price and Joe Glaser looked mad at me, "You'll never get it. Now, Chief, what would you want for location jobs?" I told him the price. He said, "You'll never get it." "Now what kind of price would you want to make records?" I told him and he said you'll never get it. But between what I wanted and what he was going to pay, we got down to the least or the most common denominator according to the way you look at it. So I finally found myself with Louie. And once more I go to Karnak and I was fitted out for a uniforms and I had to take shots by Dr. Shiffs who travels with the band now and I got my uniforms, I took my twelve shots because we were on our way -- my first job with Louie was in Bermuda and we arrived in Bermuda and low and behold we had a rehearsal at the theater where we were going to play, we were going to play only about three days, and that was for my benefit because I wanted to know what kind of program they want to show me -- what kind of program. I know most of the tunes they were going to do anyway. So they asked me, what are you going to do as your specialty. If I did "Wabash Blues,"

with the plunger.

To make a long story short, here comes the show and we play the show and then it was time for my solo, my single solo and I'm out in front and I did my "Wabash" and after the show we all went into Louis in the huge band room and this is the words that Mrs. Armstrong, Lucille said to me, "Chief, this is the Louie ever stayed on the bandstand to hear you. The first time, because most of the time when anybody played a specialty he comes into his dressing room and he lays down. But he stayed right there to hear you." And for the great Armstrong to take me in his wings like that, listen to what I wanted to do, was a great feeling. "And another thing, Chief, I never seen Louie's eyes buck out like that when you were playing that solo with the plunger. His eyes were sticking out like lamps," and it was nice. It was very nice; good reception. My second time around with Louie with the All Stars.

And we had Billy Kyle
Arvell Shaw, Joe Darensbourg, Danny Barcelona, we had Jules Brown singing -- beautiful group.
